name: OH-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by roughly 21 points at the presidential level
Jim Jordan holds a massive financial edge: about $6 million on hand versus $465 for the Democratic nominee
Jordan is a high-profile incumbent with no outside spending against him and no competitive polling history
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at only about 4 percent
model.rationale: The seat sits in a deeply Republican-leaning district, and Jordan combines incumbency, name recognition, and an overwhelming money advantage over a challenger who has raised almost nothing. With no polls or expert ratings signaling competitiveness and markets giving Democrats roughly a 4 percent chance, every available signal points to a comfortable Republican hold.
model.watch: Any major scandal, health event, or an unusually large national Democratic wave could narrow the race, though nothing in the current evidence suggests it is in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jim Jordan seeks another term in a west-central Ohio district that leans Republican by roughly twenty points at the presidential level. He enters the fall with about $6 million on hand after raising nearly $4.8 million, while Democratic nominee Joshua Kolasinski has reported minimal fundraising and negligible cash. An independent, Tracey Tackett, is also on the ballot but shows no measurable campaign infrastructure.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give the Democratic side roughly a four percent chance of winning. The district's strong Republican lean, Jordan's incumbency and national profile, and the lopsided money gap all point in the same direction. Barring an unforeseen development, the seat is expected to remain in Republican hands by a wide margin in November.
